newsitem.title: USA: Copley in plea agreement with Massachussetts.
newsitem.headline: Copley in plea agreement with Massachussetts.

text.p: Copley Pharmaceutical Inc. said Wednesday its directors voted to enter into a plea agreement covering the manufacture of four drugs investigated by the Massachusetts U.S. Attorney for nearly three years.
The state attorney is recommending a $10.65 million fine, the first levied against a company in a food and drug case under new, stricter federal guidelines, Copley said.
The fine will be paid in three instalments over a period of two years, it said.
Copley said it will take an after-tax charge of $2 million, or 10 cents per share, in the second quarter to boost its reserve for product recall and litigation expenses.
The agreement covers criminal violations arising out of changes that Copley made prior to July 1994 in the manufacturing processes of four drugs regulated by the Food and Drug Administration.

Copley admitted that batch records for two drugs -- Brompheril tablets, an over-the-counter cough and cold product, and potassium chloride tablets -- were incorrect. It also agreed that it failed to note, in reports filed annually with the FDA, production changes in those drugs and two other products.
A federal judge in Boston will be asked to accept the plea, Copley said.

The company, based in Canton, Mass., also said it entered into an agreement with the FDA providing for an independent audit of 20 of Copley's abbreviated new drug applications that have been approved.
Copley's stock fell 12.5 cents to $6.50 on Nasdaq in late morning trading.
